blocks.content: The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the country. Every authority — Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary — derives its power from it. For RRB exams, questions are mostly direct and fact-based, so this chapter focuses on high-yield exam points.
The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the country.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution is the supreme law of India, serving as the source of power for the Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary.
India has the longest written Constitution in the world.
It serves as a fundamental legal document defining government structure, distributing powers, guaranteeing Fundamental Rights, and establishing the rule of law.
Exam preparation for RRB requires a focus on direct, high-yield fact-based points.
RRB exams frequently test factual details regarding India having the longest written Constitution in the world.
Remember that all three authorities—Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary—derive their power directly from the Constitution.
Fundamental Rights and the rule of law are core components established by the Indian Constitution.

blocks.content:
A Constitution is the fundamental legal document that:
• Defines the structure of government
• Distributes powers between different organs
• Guarantees Fundamental Rights
• Establishes rule of law

India follows a written Constitution, which is the longest in the world.
